---
title: "Probably good and probably bad"
format:
  html:
    page-layout: full
execute:
  echo: false
---

Besides 1 (good) and 4 (bad), the input uses 2 (probably good) and 3
(probably bad). This site counts 3 as bad and 2 as good, so a 3 is already
in the comparison and in the delayed mode estimate, and a 2 is not visible
apart from good. nrtqclib writes only 1 or 4, never either value, so it
cannot agree with them value for value. What can be asked is whether a 2 or
a 3 looks like a delayed mode flag, and whether nrtqclib fails the same
observations.

The data cannot say who set a flag, the producer's automated QC or an
operator, and the regional centres' replies do not say which of their
tests write 3 rather than 4. The figure and tables give the signs instead:
the data mode of the observation itself, the group its profile is filed
under, how much of the profile carries the flag, and what nrtqclib made of
it.

**The groups are those of the
[Delayed mode in NRT products](analyses-data-mode.qmd) page**: declared
delayed mode, estimated delayed mode, and NRT (or no data mode), each
variable judged apart. Like that page, this one covers the profiles at sea
of the NRT products; the counts of every product, CORA and land profiles
included, are on [Input QC flags](analyses-input-flags.qmd).

```{ojs}
//| output: false
app = import(new URL("assets/js/app.js", document.baseURI).href)
meta = app.loadAnalyses()
name = (id) => app.datasetName(meta, id)
table = app.analysisTable
byDataset = (a, b) => app.datasetOrder(meta, a.dataset_id) - app.datasetOrder(meta, b.dataset_id)
rule = meta ? meta.rules.estimated_delayed : null
variableLabel = (n) => meta.variables.find((v) => v.name === n)?.label ?? n
variableOrder = (n) => meta.variables.findIndex((v) => v.name === n)
byDatasetVariable = (a, b) => byDataset(a, b) || variableOrder(a.variable) - variableOrder(b.variable)
percent = (value) => `${Math.round(100 * value)}%`
flagName = (f) => app.flagWithMeaning(f)
byProbable = (a, b) => byDatasetVariable(a, b) || a.flag - b.flag
probableObs = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("dm_probable_obs") : null
probableProfiles = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("dm_probable_profiles") : null
```

```{ojs}
meta === null ? app.analysesMissing() : html``
```

## Where they end up

```{ojs}
meta ? app.analysisFigure(
  "dm_probable",
  "Every observation the input flags 2 (probably good) or 3 (probably bad), by where it ends up: in a profile that declares delayed mode, in one the estimate files as delayed mode, or in an NRT profile (or one with no data mode), split by whether nrtqclib flags the observation bad too. One panel per variable and flag; the number at the end of a bar is the observations it is made of, so a bar of a few dozen says little. Purple and orange are the flags that look like delayed mode; blue and grey are left in the NRT comparison.",
  "Stacked bars per product, for each variable and flag 2 or 3, of the share of the flagged observations in declared or estimated delayed mode profiles or in NRT profiles."
) : html``
```

The tables below give the same observations with more detail.

## Where they are

For each flag, the share of its observations whose own data mode is
delayed, the share in profiles filed under declared or estimated delayed
mode, and the share nrtqclib flags bad.

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// One row per product, variable and flag, summed over the observation table.
probableRows = probableObs
  ? [...probableObs.reduce((m, r) => {
      const key = `${r.dataset_id}|${r.variable}|${r.flag}`;
      const row = m.get(key) ?? { key, dataset_id: r.dataset_id, variable: r.variable, flag: r.flag, n_obs: 0, n_dm_delayed: 0, n_group_delayed: 0, n_nrtqclib_bad: 0 };
      row.n_obs += r.n_obs;
      if (r.obs_data_mode === "D") row.n_dm_delayed += r.n_obs;
      if (r.group === "delayed" || r.group === "estimated_delayed") row.n_group_delayed += r.n_obs;
      if (r.nrtqclib_bad) row.n_nrtqclib_bad += r.n_obs;
      m.set(key, row);
      return m;
    }, new Map()).values()].sort(byProbable)
  : []
```

```{ojs}
meta ? table(probableRows, [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "variable", label: "Variable", align: "left", format: variableLabel },
  { key: "flag", label: "Input flag", align: "left", format: flagName },
  { key: "n_obs", label: "Observations" },
  { key: "n_dm_delayed", label: "Delayed mode observations", title: "Share whose own data mode column says delayed mode (D)", format: (_, r) => app.formatSmallShare(r.n_dm_delayed, r.n_obs) },
  { key: "n_group_delayed", label: "In delayed or estimated profiles", title: "Share in profiles filed under declared or estimated delayed mode for this variable", format: (_, r) => app.formatSmallShare(r.n_group_delayed, r.n_obs) },
  { key: "n_nrtqclib_bad", label: "nrtqclib flags bad", title: "Share nrtqclib flags 4 (bad)", format: (_, r) => app.formatSmallShare(r.n_nrtqclib_bad, r.n_obs) }
]) : html``
```

## How they sit in their profiles

```{ojs}
meta ? md`An operator who doubts a cast tends to flag most of it; an automated test tends to flag a point or a stretch. "Most of the profile" uses the measure of the delayed mode estimate: the flag on at least ${percent(rule.min_share)} of the variable's observations with a usable input flag, counted only with at least ${rule.min_observations} of them. The last column is those still filed as NRT, or with no data mode: for a 3 that is because nrtqclib fails the same observations, so they are not the input's alone and the estimate does not take them; a 2 is never counted by it.` : html``
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// One row per product, variable and flag, summed over the groups, keeping
// apart the profiles flagged almost throughout that are still filed as NRT.
profileRows = probableProfiles
  ? [...probableProfiles.reduce((m, r) => {
      const key = `${r.dataset_id}|${r.variable}|${r.flag}`;
      const row = m.get(key) ?? { key, dataset_id: r.dataset_id, variable: r.variable, flag: r.flag, n_profiles: 0, n_profiles_single: 0, n_profiles_most: 0, n_most_nrt: 0 };
      row.n_profiles += r.n_profiles;
      row.n_profiles_single += r.n_profiles_single;
      row.n_profiles_most += r.n_profiles_most;
      if (r.group === "nrt" || r.group === "unknown") row.n_most_nrt += r.n_profiles_most;
      m.set(key, row);
      return m;
    }, new Map()).values()].sort(byProbable)
  : []
```

```{ojs}
meta ? table(profileRows, [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "variable", label: "Variable", align: "left", format: variableLabel },
  { key: "flag", label: "Input flag", align: "left", format: flagName },
  { key: "n_profiles", label: "Profiles", title: "Profiles at sea with at least one observation flagged this value" },
  { key: "n_profiles_single", label: "One observation", title: "Share of those profiles with this flag on a single observation", format: (_, r) => app.formatShare(r.n_profiles_single, r.n_profiles) },
  { key: "n_profiles_most", label: "Most of the profile", title: "Profiles with this flag on most of the profile, by the estimate's measure" },
  { key: "n_most_nrt", label: "Of those, still NRT", title: "Profiles flagged almost throughout that are filed as NRT or data mode unknown" }
]) : html``
```

## Which nrtqclib checks fail them

Of the observations flagged 2 or 3 that nrtqclib flags bad, the share each
of its checks failed. An observation can fail more than one, so a row can
add up to more than 100%. A salinity value fails "Temperature flag carried
over" when the temperature beside it failed.

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// The nrtqclib checks behind the observations it flags bad, as a share of
// them. A check that judges the profile or its pressure counts for both
// variables.
failColumns = probableObs
  ? Object.keys(probableObs[0] ?? {}).filter((k) => k.startsWith("fail_"))
  : []
checkRows = probableObs
  ? [...probableObs.filter((r) => r.nrtqclib_bad).reduce((m, r) => {
      const key = `${r.dataset_id}|${r.variable}|${r.flag}`;
      const row = m.get(key) ?? { key, dataset_id: r.dataset_id, variable: r.variable, flag: r.flag, n_bad: 0, ...Object.fromEntries(failColumns.map((c) => [c, 0])) };
      row.n_bad += r.n_obs;
      for (const c of failColumns) row[c] += r[c] ?? 0;
      m.set(key, row);
      return m;
    }, new Map()).values()].sort(byProbable)
  : []
usedChecks = failColumns.filter((c) => checkRows.some((r) => r[c] > 0))
```

```{ojs}
meta ? table(checkRows, [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "variable", label: "Variable", align: "left", format: variableLabel },
  { key: "flag", label: "Input flag", align: "left", format: flagName },
  { key: "n_bad", label: "nrtqclib bad" },
  ...usedChecks.map((c) => ({
    key: c,
    label: app.qcCheck(`qc_${c.slice(5)}`).label,
    format: (_, r) => app.formatSmallShare(r[c], r.n_bad)
  }))
]) : html``
```

## Read together

The products differ:

- **Arctic NRT regional**: the 2s and 3s are delayed mode flags. Every one
  is on an observation whose own data mode is delayed, and nrtqclib rarely
  fails them.
- **Arctic NRT global**: few of the 3s are on delayed mode observations,
  but most are in profiles the estimate files as delayed mode, and nearly
  every one of those profiles carries the 3 almost throughout. These look
  like an operator's. The 3s left in NRT profiles are scattered, often one
  to a profile.
- **Mediterranean NRT global**: the 3s are on observations marked real
  time. In temperature they rarely cover a whole profile, and nrtqclib
  fails much of them, mostly by its regional range check, which points to
  an automated range test on the producer's side that marks its result
  probably bad; the temperature profiles flagged 3 almost throughout stay
  NRT because nrtqclib fails them too. Salinity is mixed: a large part of
  its 3s are in profiles the estimate files as delayed mode, and those
  nrtqclib fails are mostly out of its global and regional ranges.
- **Baltic NRT regional**: the few 3s are mostly single observations.

The 2s are close to good everywhere: nrtqclib rarely fails them.
